output.brief: Pellacott's 2026-built VA-220 valves are failing, and the cause is not the new installers or firmware 4.2. The Quality Lab matched claims by serial number. Pellacott valves fail at the same rate (about 40 per 1,000) regardless of installer or firmware. Durrant-Hale valves stay at 5–7 per 1,000 in every group. A helium retest of unused warehouse stock found 11% of Pellacott's 2026 valves leaking at the seat. The independent calibration visit found Pellacott's only VA-220 leak rig out of service since 9 Jan 2026, with no VA-220 test program on any other rig. Certificate tables repeat four sequences that also appear in 2025 certificates, so the certificates do not reflect tests that were done. The score rose because complete-looking certificates earn credit, which is how the score and the failures moved in opposite directions. Do not release the six held lots on fresh certificates. Quarantine 2026 Pellacott stock, suspend dock-to-stock, and release stock only after Brenmoor's own helium testing. Hold the installer remediation plan and the chargebacks. Then audit other suppliers' test records, and make scoring credit test records only when rig logs or witnessed tests back them. The seal supplier and Line 3 effects can't be separated yet, so treat them as open and have Pellacott's change reviewed.
